text.text_excerpt: I really enjoyed this place! I eat Vietnamese fairly often, and I would say this ranks among the best I have eaten in a while. I ordered the tofu vermicelli and the bay shrimp spring rolls. Both were tasty and large in size! The restaurant is located right next to the Louisiana Supreme Court house, so it was really convenient to get to after a long day walking around the French Quarter. Inside, the atmosphere is quiet and quaint, which is a nice escape from the noise outside. The restaurant is pretty clean and has good air condition, which is critical in the heat and humidity in the summer. If you prefer, they also have outdoor patio seating.

I had lunch here on a whim, and was very satisfied with the experience. The food is excellent, service is fairly quick, and the prices, for what you get, are reasonable. One of the stand-out features of this place is its setting: right on Exchange Alley, and very near the wonderful sweet shop, Sucre. I chose one of the patio tables beneath a giant shade umbrella, where a few feet away a painter was at work outside his studio. Such a pleasant way to relax and refuel. I ordered the yellow curry with tofu, made medium spicy. There was A LOT of tofu, which made me very happy, and it was fried the way I like it. You may be asking, Vietnamese in New Orleans, why would one skip out on all the delicious Cajun food? Well, I guess one can only eat it for so many meals and or days straight before you need a break honestly. My fall back is always Vietnamese and will go out of my way to find a good one if possible. Nine Roses Cafe was a delightful experience, quaint, good food, reasonable prices, and centrally located. As mentioned above, Nine Roses Cafe is centrally located, right within the French Quarter, so if you need your Vietnamese fix, look no further.
